description:
Your family demanded half of your $50,000 lottery win, not knowing it was really $340 million. A POV money story about a lottery winner, family money and a brother-in-law who sued for half of the wrong number.

You're a 911 dispatcher in Marietta, Georgia. Once a year, on your late dad's birthday, you buy one Mega Millions ticket with his numbers. This year all six numbers hit. You tell the family group chat a smaller, true prize: four numbers and the Mega Ball, fifty grand. At Mom's birthday, your brother-in-law Trevor announces that in this family windfalls get split, and asks for $25,000 by December first. Then his lawyer sends a letter: half of the prize, because Trevor handed you five dollars for a ticket. What Trevor doesn't know: his five dollars bought his own quick pick, you kept both receipts, the store camera saw everything, and his house goes up for auction the day after the meeting.

Real lottery numbers: lump sum vs annuity, why the $340 million jackpot is $157 million in cash, the 24% withholding and the 37% bill that comes in April, how an anonymous lottery winner claims through a trust in Georgia, and who legally owns a lottery ticket in an office pool or family pool. Plus a foreclosure "sale under power", a $71,000 gambling secret, and how a dispatcher had $118,000 saved before the ticket with a 457(b) and a Roth IRA. Personal finance and financial literacy for anyone whose family has a plan for their money.

🔑 5 money rules
1. Before you tell anyone, tell a lawyer.
2. Plan for the tax bill before you spend the check.
3. Show people a twenty before you show them a hundred.
4. Pay the bill, not the person.
5. If money is pooled, put it in writing the same day.

Never lend your name. A co-signer owes every dollar.
Never chase a loss. You only double it.
When family is drowning, help with a plan, not a payment.
